To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new 2D Cd(ii) metal organic framework has been synthesized and characterized.
we synthesized and characterized two new MOFs with different topologies and luminescence properties and demonstrated that one of them, a Cd(ii) LUMOF, can be used as a sensor for picric acid.
we have synthesized a new Cd(ii) luminal MOF, which is highly selective and sensitive towards TNP in aqueous phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and synthesis of a luminescent LMOF, which has been demonstrated to be a highly sensitive and selective sensor for TNP in aqueous media, and the LMOF coated strip is an effective tool for the detection of TNP.

the design, synthesis and characterization of a new family of Cd(ii) L MOF, which is an efficient fluorescent sensor in the selective detection of TNP in aqueous media and also in the detection of TNP by the Cd(ii)LMOF coated paper strips.

the synthesis and characterisation of new mixed ligand Cd(ii) and Ni(ii) metal organic framework materials, their luminescent properties and their use as a selective fluorescent probe for the detection of picric acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a Cd(ii) LUMO is an excellent fluorescent probe for TNP detection and the sensing mechanism is a combination of both electron transfer and energy transfer processes.
the present work demonstrates a facile, rapid, and selective detection of TNP in aqueous media by a Cd(ii) LUMOF.
the present work is an important step in the direction of developing a simple paper strip based fluorescence sensor for the detection of TNP in aqueous media.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have synthesized a new Cd(ii) LUMOFS and a Ni(ii) MOF with 5 bromoisophthalic acid and a flexible tripodal ligands.
the Cd(ii) MOFs are luminescent sensors and the Cd(ii) LUMOF is an efficient and selective sensor for TNP over other electron deficient and electron rich nitroanalytes.

the Cd(ii) MOFs are efficient luminescent probes for detection of picrate in aqueous media, and this work may be useful in designing new materials for the detection and sensing of nitroanalytic compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cd(ii) LMF can be used for the selective detection of TNP in the presence of other nitro analyte in aqueous phase, which can be further developed into paper strip sensor.
a Cd(ii) LUMO F coated paper strip can be used for the selective detection of TNP in aqueous solution.

a simple and inexpensive paper strip coated with the LMOF can be used for the rapid and sensitive detection of TNP in the presence of a variety of nitro compounds in aqueous solution, which has potential applications in environmental analysis.
